connections.why: Electron arrangement explains the order and groups of the Periodic Table
Atoms transfer electrons to reach stable outer shells, forming ions
Sharing outer electrons lets atoms reach a full shell without forming ions
Electrolysis splits ionic compounds because their ions become mobile when molten or in solution
Particle behaviour underpins separating mixtures by distillation and filtration
Mole calculations are the basis of titration analysis
Group 1 trends follow directly from the table's structure
Group 7 reactivity trends follow from position in the table
Halogens add across the double bond in alkene addition reactions
A metal's place in the reactivity series determines how it is extracted
The most reactive metals must be extracted by electrolysis
Neutralisation reactions are used to prepare soluble salts by titration
Tests for ions rely on the characteristic reactions of ionic compounds
Activation energy links energy profiles to how fast reactions go
Equilibrium is reached when forward and reverse rates are equal
Carbon's four covalent bonds underpin the whole of organic chemistry
Crude oil fractions are mostly alkanes separated by distillation
Cracking long alkanes produces shorter alkanes and useful alkenes
Alkene monomers join by addition to make poly(alkene) polymers
Oxidising alcohols produces carboxylic acids
Alcohols react with carboxylic acids to form esters
Carboxylic acids are a reactant in esterification
Combustion of alkane fuels is a key exothermic reaction
